definitions.explanation: The point at which symptoms of a disease or condition first appear.

examples.japanese: {発症|はっしょう}から{三日|みっか}で{入院|にゅういん}した。
examples.english: I was hospitalized three days after the onset.

examples.japanese: {糖尿病|とうにょうびょう}を{発症|はっしょう}するリスクが{高|たか}い。
examples.english: There's a high risk of developing diabetes.

examples.japanese: ストレスが{発症|はっしょう}の{引|ひ}き{金|がね}になることがある。
examples.english: Stress can trigger the onset of the condition.

notes:
{発症|はっしょう} refers specifically to the moment when symptoms of a disease first appear. Common in medical and health-related contexts.

COMPOUND: {発|はつ} (emit/appear) + {症|しょう} (symptom)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {発症|はっしょう}する: to develop (a disease)
- {発症|はっしょう}{率|りつ}: incidence rate
- {発症|はっしょう}{時期|じき}: time of onset
- {発症|はっしょう}リスク: risk of onset
- {発症|はっしょう}を{防|ふせ}ぐ: to prevent onset
- {発症|はっしょう}から～{日|にち}: ~ days after onset

WATCH OUT:
Not to be confused with {発祥|はっしょう} (origin, birthplace of something).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {発病|はつびょう}: falling ill (broader; emphasizes becoming sick rather than symptom onset)
- {再発|さいはつ}: recurrence, relapse
